hyperedges.label: Platform layer as the bridge between the two documentation communities
Flicker-free render pipeline (lex once, fill grid, compose one frame)
Four-function platform contract, declared once and defined twice
Option surface: each option reaches exactly one place in the program

nodes.label: Cross-community bridge node (documentation-only abstraction)
nodes.rationale: The platform-layer node bridges two communities over exactly two of its seven edges, and it has file_type rationale rather than code: no equivalent node exists on the AST side, and in hackertyper.c the four functions scatter across three code communities, so the abstraction is documentation-only and has no structural existence the AST can see.

nodes.label: Documented Design Concepts (graph community)
nodes.rationale: Community holding design-intent nodes. term_key lands here rather than in the platform community because it also carries user-facing behaviour (the timed ESC read, and a link to the placard), and the single-file zero-dependency constraint sits here as the rationale that forces the four-function seam to exist.

nodes.label: Documented Platform Layer (graph community)
nodes.rationale: Community holding the platform-layer documentation nodes: the Windows and POSIX backends plus term_enter, term_leave and term_size stay inside it, which is why five of the bridge node's seven edges never cross a community boundary.

nodes.label: Cell grid (screen model)
nodes.rationale: A grid of Cell (char + tone) with a cursor and a scroll. It is deliberately one row shorter than the terminal because the last row belongs to the status bar.

nodes.label: Single-fwrite frame composition (Buf)
nodes.rationale: The whole frame is composed into a single growable Buf and written with one fwrite per keystroke - cursor home, every row with colour changes coalesced into runs, the status bar, then the placard if one is up. One write means no flicker and no partial frames.

nodes.label: paint (startup lexer)
nodes.rationale: Walks the payload once at startup and writes one tone byte per source byte, so highlighting is free at render time - a byte already knows its own colour. The classifier handles block and line comments, string and character literals with escapes, numbers, and two keyword tables.

nodes.label: screen_putc
nodes.rationale: The only way text enters the grid, so it can own wrapping, tab expansion, newlines, and memmove-based scroll-up in one place instead of having those rules duplicated at every caller.

nodes.label: slurp (payload file reader)
nodes.rationale: Reads the file named by --file so its contents stand in for payload_builtin; it is the single place --file reaches.

nodes.label: Status bar
nodes.rationale: Owns the terminal's last row, which is why the Cell grid is one row shorter than the terminal; it is appended to the frame after the rows.

nodes.label: tone_ansi (tone-to-ANSI emitter)
nodes.rationale: The only reader of the mono flag: colour suppression happens at emit time rather than by skipping the lexer, which keeps the rest of the pipeline identical in both modes.

nodes.label: Parallel tone byte array
nodes.rationale: One tone byte per source byte - keyword, type, string, comment, number, preprocessor, punctuation - computed once at startup so render time never classifies anything. It is still built under --mono; the values are simply discarded.

nodes.label: hackertyper
nodes.rationale: A terminal homage to hackertyper.net delivered as one C file with no dependencies: mashing any key streams plausible, syntax-highlighted systems code three characters at a time.

nodes.label: --file PATH option
nodes.rationale: Types out PATH instead of the built-in payload: it sends slurp to read PATH in place of payload_builtin. The lexer then paints whatever came back exactly as it paints the built-in reel, so a C file arrives highlighted and a plain text file arrives green - one substitution at the source, no special-casing downstream.

nodes.label: --mono option
nodes.rationale: Single-colour output with no syntax highlighting. It sets one flag that only tone_ansi reads: the lexer still runs and the tone array is still built, so the colours are computed and then thrown away. That is why mono costs nothing to switch on, and why it collapses every colour run in the frame into a single run.

nodes.label: --speed N option
nodes.rationale: Sets the reveal count (1-64, default 3): the loop bound deciding how many characters screen_putc receives per keystroke. It is clamped, so a fat-fingered --speed 5000 degrades to a very fast crank rather than a buffer overrun.

nodes.label: Built-in payload (fictional fabric/quantum_lane.c)
nodes.rationale: The reel is a fictional fabric/quantum_lane.c - a credit-based packet lane scheduler with sibling hand-off - syntactically honest C and semantically invented, so there is no such fabric, no such API and nothing to look up. Swappable with --file.

nodes.label: ACCESS GRANTED / ACCESS DENIED placard
nodes.rationale: TAB three times raises ACCESS GRANTED and BACKSPACE three times raises ACCESS DENIED, standing in for the original site's triple CAPS LOCK and triple ALT because a terminal cannot see bare modifier keys. Any other key dismisses it.

nodes.label: hackertyper.net (original site)
nodes.rationale: The site this program is an homage to. It uses triple CAPS LOCK and triple ALT; a terminal cannot see bare modifier keys, so TAB and BACKSPACE stand in for them.

nodes.label: Colour run coalescing
nodes.rationale: Rows are emitted with colour changes coalesced into runs, so an escape sequence is written only where the tone actually changes. Under --mono every run in the frame collapses into a single run.

nodes.label: Keyboard as a crank (keystrokes reveal, never interpret)
nodes.norm_label: keyboard as a crank (keystrokes reveal, never interpret)
nodes.rationale: Nothing typed is ever interpreted: the keyboard is a crank and the payload is the reel. Any printable key reveals the next N characters; ESC or Ctrl-C restores the terminal and exits.

nodes.label: Resize handling at the top of the loop
nodes.norm_label: resize handling at the top of the loop
nodes.rationale: Checked at the top of the loop rather than in a signal handler: if the terminal changed size the grid is reallocated and cleared, and typing continues from the same payload offset.

nodes.label: restore_terminal (idempotent, atexit)
nodes.rationale: Registered with atexit and made idempotent so a signal, an exit(), or the normal path all leave the terminal usable - and the farewell line survives the second call.

nodes.label: term_enter
nodes.rationale: The single gate into terminal manipulation (raw mode, hidden cursor); because --help returns before it, that path has nothing to restore.

nodes.label: term_key
nodes.rationale: Supplies one key per turn of the crank: _getch on Windows, and on POSIX a timed read that distinguishes a bare ESC from the start of an arrow-key sequence.

nodes.label: term_leave
nodes.rationale: The platform-specific half of leaving the terminal as it was found; the idempotent restore path wraps it.

nodes.label: term_size
nodes.rationale: Reports the terminal dimensions (TIOCGWINSZ on POSIX) so the loop can notice a resize before composing a frame.

nodes.label: --help option
nodes.rationale: Prints the usage text and returns before term_enter, so it is the one path through the program that never touches the terminal - no raw mode, no hidden cursor, nothing to restore.

nodes.label: Platform layer (four-function abstraction)
nodes.rationale: All platform difference is confined to two implementations of the same four functions - term_enter, term_leave, term_size, term_key - so the rest of the program is platform-agnostic.

nodes.label: POSIX terminal backend
nodes.rationale: Implements the four functions with termios (ECHO/ICANON/ISIG cleared), TIOCGWINSZ, and a timed read that tells a bare ESC from the start of an arrow-key sequence.

nodes.label: Windows terminal backend
nodes.rationale: Implements the four functions with ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING, UTF-8 output, and _getch, so ANSI frames work in a Windows console without a separate renderer.

nodes.label: Four-function contract block (single declaration above the #ifdef)
nodes.norm_label: four-function contract block (single declaration above the #ifdef)
nodes.rationale: The four signatures are declared once above the #ifdef and defined twice below it, so each backend is checked against one signature instead of declaring its own: a backend that drops a function or changes a parameter list fails to build on its own platform rather than staying silent until somebody compiles on the other one. Verified both ways on MSVC (error C2129 pointing at the contract block; warning C4029 plus error C2198 at call sites) and reported by GCC/Clang as -Wundefined-internal and a conflicting-types error.

nodes.label: Single-file, zero-dependency design
nodes.rationale: Everything lives in one C file with no dependencies, so the whole program builds from a single translation unit on POSIX (make), MSVC (cl), or MinGW (gcc) with nothing to fetch or link.
